scope: Development evaluation of training-reference library, nominal and identified plants; not independent held-out robustness
primary_selection_rule: Use all five common seeds; keep the earlier two-seed pilot as a repeat check, never pool it as additional training seeds

conditions.checkpoint: last.pt / EMA policy in unchanged local evaluator
conditions.velocity_definition: world XYZ root-origin linear velocity, per-component RMSE on available valid samples

provenance_limits: Archive contains no evaluated checkpoint, source, parameter or motion hashes; remote runtime identity is not independently bound to each result.
Previously imported training metadata supplies expected checkpoint hashes, not proof that those exact bytes were evaluated remotely.
One repeat per clip with fixed evaluation seed. Pilot/common outcomes differ for some A0/A clips; cause not established.
RMSE uses each policy valid duration; early failure shortens coverage, so RMSE alone is not an equal-duration comparison.
Motion clips are not independent training seeds.

code_findings.fact: A+/B/C world models fit frozen CPU paired data; A0/A fit online replay windows.
A0/A normalizers update online; paired-path normalizers initialize from fit pairs and are not updated during online collection.
Paired-path forward supervision spans 32 steps; base uses wm_window=8 and different error-floor/masking behavior.
A+ raw-action matched inputs already fail, before adding the explicit effort path or C response penalty.

inference: Results localize the collapse to changes shared from A+ onward; frozen-data coverage, normalization, objective horizon, context and CPU/GPU consistency are hypotheses, not isolated causes.
next_steps: Preserve checkpoints and both evaluation sessions; do not pool pilot/common or rerun unchanged eight-hour queues.
Record remote input/checkpoint fingerprints and repeat A0/A evaluations before interpreting small calibration differences.
Test an A control against an A+ raw-action model fitted on online replay with matched loss horizon/normalizers, using a new protocol and fresh attempt; recover stable A+ before adding B and then C.
Keep response test and D/C-perm locked until data/response validity and calibration criteria are met.
